title: Moving Beyond Binary Measures of Gender in Political Ambition

selected_claim.evidence_location: Table 1, Model 2 (Gendered Personality), in “Testing Gendered Personality and Ambition”; measure and model description in “Research Design.”
selected_claim.evidence_summary: In the ordered logit model of having thought about running for office, masculinity has a positive, statistically significant coefficient (3.18, robust SE 0.54, p < 0.01). Higher masculinity scores are associated with greater odds of reporting a higher ambition category, conditional on the model’s measured covariates.
selected_claim.x: Respondent’s short Bem Sex Roles Inventory masculinity index, an additive scale rescaled from 0 (least identified with the traits) to 1 (most identified with the traits).
selected_claim.y: Respondent’s reported prior consideration of running for political office, measured in three ordered categories: never thought about it, has crossed my mind, or thought about it many times.
selected_claim.target_population: The 800 respondents in the original Lucid Theorem survey gathered on May 18, 2023; the paper describes the sample as balanced on sex and partisanship.
selected_claim.adjustment_description: Table 1, Model 2 adjusts for femininity, sex (Woman), strength of partisanship, education, age, and race (Nonwhite).
selected_claim.mixed_methods_boundary: The survey included a separate randomized prompt experiment in an unrelated knowledge battery. The extracted claim is supported by the separate observational ordered-logit estimate in Table 1, Model 2: masculinity was measured, not randomized. The paper reports that the ambition measures were statistically indistinguishable between the experimental prompt groups.

evidence_summary: The focal paper examines whether self-ascribed masculinity, measured with a short Bem Sex Roles Inventory masculinity index rescaled from 0 to 1, is associated with reported prior consideration of running for political office in ordered categories (never, crossed my mind, thought about it many times). The provided claim describes an observational survey of 800 Lucid Theorem respondents collected May 18, 2023, balanced on sex and partisanship. Table 1, Model 2 adjusts for femininity, sex, strength of partisanship, education, age, and race.

link_reviews.note: The exposure-side findings concern training or educational participation linked to assertiveness; the outcome-side findings concern political classroom exercises or skills programs linked to ambition. These are specific educational experiences rather than formal attainment, so the evidence is not identical to the paper’s education control, but both links fit the unit’s broad education-and-training category. No split is needed.

confounders.reason: The focal Model 2 includes Education as a pre-treatment control (inventory entry c3), and the paper measures it as educational attainment on a seven-category scale. This is a direct control for formal attainment, though it may not capture educational quality, field of study, or specific training and classroom experiences.

No supported confounding path: every finding on this confounder's link to the exposure was excluded, so it cannot confound the focal relationship. This status was set from the findings alone; the paper's specification was not reviewed for it.

limitations: The snapshot's focal variables are represented by the reported masculinity score and nascent political ambition; the specific survey coding and Lucid Theorem sample are not themselves generalizable measures.
The outcome is retrospective reported consideration, not actual candidacy or officeholding.
The claim is observational and adjusted only for the listed covariates; causal interpretation may remain vulnerable to residual confounding and temporal ambiguity.
